owner.name: Meet Jethwa
owner.headline: Small, sharp Mac apps that *stay on your device.*
owner.bio: I build native tools that do one job well: recording guides, keeping snippets, fixing posture, deciding what to buy. Most run entirely on your Mac.
owner.cta: Using one of these? *Tell me what's missing.*

apps.name: Tapri
apps.tagline: Ten Mac utilities in one native app.
apps.description: Each utility is named for a spice in a cup of masala chai. Switch on the ones you want; anything left off holds no timers and costs nothing.
highlights: Menu bar, clipboard, windows, system monitor, screenshot & OCR, and five more
One menu bar item, one process, one thing to update
Four spices free forever

apps.name: Stepwise
apps.description: Stepwise watches you do a task and writes it up: every click becomes a captioned, screenshotted step you can export as a PDF.
highlights: Captions written from what you actually clicked
Keeps the screen recording beside the guide
Your screen never leaves your Mac

apps.name: Cadence
apps.tagline: Screen guides in 5 steps, 1 minute each.
apps.description: A screen recorder that will not let you ramble. Each step auto-stops at 60 seconds, then everything is stitched into one MP4.
highlights: Outline your steps, then record against the clock
Exports one MP4 with title cards and chapter markers
No timeline, no editing, no cloud

apps.name: Pickwise
apps.tagline: Which one should I buy? Ask once.
apps.description: Give Pickwise two to five products and it compares current price, specs and trade-offs, then commits to one verdict with the reasoning.
highlights: A comparison table with honest pros and cons
One answer instead of thirty tabs of research
Coming to iPhone

apps.name: CodeMate
apps.tagline: Interview prep that feels like an IDE, not a website.
apps.description: A native Mac app for DSA and system-design prep, with a guided roadmap so you always know what is next.
highlights: Real test-case grading for Swift, Python and JavaScript, run locally
On-device AI assistant: no API key, no per-message cost
A whiteboard for LLD and HLD questions

apps.name: Cubby
apps.tagline: Your stuff, in its place. One keystroke away.
apps.description: A menu-bar vault for the things you paste every day. Press a hotkey, type to filter, hit return, and it is copied.
highlights: Named compartments for phone numbers, API keys and bank details
Secrets backed by the macOS Keychain
No accounts, no servers, no telemetry

apps.name: Cairn
apps.description: Desk wellness for macOS. Cairn reads your posture, eyes and screen distance through the webcam and nudges you before the slump sets in.
highlights: Tracks eye strain, screen distance and slouching
A stretch coach that follows your form
Every frame analysed on-device; nothing recorded or uploaded

apps.name: Brahma Muhurat
apps.tagline: The 48 minutes before dawn, timed for where you are.
apps.description: Brahma Muhurat begins 1 hour 36 minutes before sunrise. The app works out that window for your location, along with the rest of the day's light.
highlights: Timings for today, tomorrow and the day after
First light, dawn, solar noon, golden hour and dusk
Moon phase tracker
